brief: Holds the expectations a service must meet, stated in operational terms, and judges them against measured numbers.
detail: An SLA is part of the design and not a dashboard threshold added after an incident. Expect names a well-known subject, response time percentiles, throughput, error rate, availability, CPU, memory, and a closer, Under, AtMost, AtLeast or Over, gives the bound; ExpectP95, ExpectMean, ExpectValue, ExpectRate and ExpectStable do the same for a metric of your own. CheckAgainst judges them against a stzPerfMonitor and returns the breaches as findings in the unified shape, subject perf, ready for stzRuleReport. An expectation over a metric the monitor does not carry is an error finding, never a silent pass. AsWarning softens the last expectation to advice. Judged values that depend on the clock, rates and CPU, should be asserted by range.
receiver:
oMon = StzPerfMonitor("api")
oT = oMon.NewTimer("http.request.ms")
oT.Record(20)
oT.Record(40)
oT.Record(60)
oT.Record(80)
oT.Record(400)
oReq = oMon.NewCounter("http.requests")
oReq.IncrementBy(200)
oErr = oMon.NewCounter("http.errors")
oErr.IncrementBy(1)
oDepth = oMon.NewGauge("queue.depth")
oDepth.Set(120)
o1 = StzSla("restolean-api")
o1.Expect(:ResponseTimeP95).Under(200)
o1.Expect(:ResponseTimeP50).AtMost(100)
o1.Expect(:Availability).AtLeast(99.9)
o1.ExpectValue("queue.depth").AtMost(100)
